high.title: IHSG Closes Up at Level 6,236 After Staying in Green Zone All Day
high.summary: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) closed up 49.76 points (+0.80%) at 6,236.12 on Friday, July 31, 2026, remaining consistently in positive territory throughout the session. Trading volume reached 32.45 billion shares with a turnover of Rp 18.25 trillion. This marks a solid end to the trading week for Indonesian equity markets.

high.title: IHSG Posts Weekly Gain of 0.64%, But Daily Transaction Value Falls Sharply by 21.86%
high.summary: The IHSG gained 0.64% over the trading week of July 27–31, 2026, closing at 6,236.126 and lifting BEI's market capitalization to Rp 10,923 trillion (+0.48%). However, average daily transaction value dropped sharply by 21.86% to Rp 15.44 trillion, signaling reduced market participation and potential liquidity concerns. Investors should monitor whether lower trading volumes persist in the coming weeks.

high.title: Finance Minister Purbaya Promises No Tax Rate Hikes, but Will Aggressively Chase Tax Evaders
high.summary: Indonesian Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa confirmed that the government will not raise tax rates but will intensify enforcement against tax leakages, manipulation, and non-compliant taxpayers to boost state revenue. The government plans to actively follow up on public reports of companies suspected of tax evasion, including in the steel sector. This policy stance is significant for businesses and investors as it signals a more aggressive tax enforcement environment without additional rate burdens.

high.title: KAI's Profit Drops Sharply — Here's the Cause
high.summary: State-owned PT Kereta Api Indonesia (KAI) recorded a steep decline in profit for H1 2026, with net profit falling to Rp 314.03 billion from Rp 1.18 trillion in H1 2025 — a drop of over 73%. The main culprit was a surge in net losses from associates and joint ventures, rising from Rp 948.20 billion to Rp 3.00 trillion, likely reflecting pressure from its high-speed rail and LRT joint venture investments. Despite revenue growing 6.6% to Rp 17.96 trillion, the massive associate losses signal significant financial stress within the KAI Group ecosystem.

high.title: New Fuel Prices at All Gas Stations: Pertamina Cuts Non-Subsidized BBM Prices from August 1
high.summary: Pertamina has reduced prices for non-subsidized fuels including Pertamax (RON 92), Pertamax Green 95 (RON 95), and Pertamax Turbo (RON 98) effective August 1, 2026, while Pertamina Dex and Dexlite prices remain unchanged. BP also cut prices for BP 92 and BP Ultimate, though BP Ultimate Diesel rose, and VIVO similarly adjusted its lineup. These price changes have broad implications for inflation, consumer spending power, and energy sector stocks in Indonesia.

high.title: Government to Accelerate Tax Debt Collection, Deploy Coretax to Plug Revenue Leakages
high.summary: Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa announced the government will intensify collection efforts against tax delinquents and leverage the Coretax software system to eliminate tax payment manipulation and revenue leakages. The Directorate General of Taxation will take a more proactive approach, including following up on public reports of tax non-compliance. This signals a tightening regulatory environment for Indonesian businesses and could significantly impact state revenue targets for 2026.

high.title: KAI's Profit Drops Sharply — Here's the Cause
high.summary: PT Kereta Api Indonesia (KAI) recorded a significant profit decline in H1 2026, with pre-tax profit falling to Rp 842.69 billion from Rp 1.86 trillion in H1 2025, and net profit dropping to Rp 314.03 billion from Rp 1.18 trillion. The main driver was a surge in net losses from associates and joint ventures, rising from Rp 948.20 billion to Rp 3.00 trillion. Despite revenue growing 6.6% to Rp 17.96 trillion, the dramatic profit erosion signals significant financial stress within KAI's broader group structure, relevant to investors in the state-owned enterprise sector.

high.title: CPO Reference Price Falls Due to Weak Global Demand
high.summary: Indonesia's Ministry of Trade has set the CPO reference price for August 2026 at US$996.52/MT, a decline of US$4.38 (0.44%) from the previous month's US$1,000.90/MT, driven by sluggish global demand. The export duty (Bea Keluar) is set at US$148/MT and the export levy (Pungutan Ekspor) at 12.5% of the reference price, equivalent to US$124.56/MT. This directly impacts the cost competitiveness and profitability of Indonesian palm oil producers and exporters.

high.title: Full List of New Fuel Prices at All Gas Stations Effective August 1
high.summary: Pertamina has cut prices for non-subsidized fuels including Pertamax (RON 92), Pertamax Green 95, and Pertamax Turbo effective August 1, 2026, while Pertamina Dex and Dexlite remain unchanged. Competing fuel retailers BP and VIVO also adjusted prices, with some gasoline grades reduced and diesel grades increased. These fuel price changes directly impact inflation, consumer purchasing power, and operating costs across multiple sectors of the Indonesian economy.

medium.title: BGN Prioritizes Local Rice for School Meal Program (MBG), Bulog Supply Serves as Reserve
medium.summary: The National Nutrition Agency (BGN) confirmed it will prioritize local food sources, including locally-sourced rice, for the government's Free School Meal Program (MBG), aiming to strengthen regional economies by empowering local farmers and SMEs. Bulog's role will be limited to acting as a buffer supplier only when local supply is insufficient or price volatility occurs. This policy has implications for agricultural supply chains, UMKM businesses, and state logistics company Bulog's revenue streams.

medium.title: B50 Biodiesel Implementation: Drivers Report No Engine Problems After One Month of Use
medium.summary: Indonesia's mandatory B50 biodiesel policy, which blends 50% palm oil into diesel fuel, has been in effect since July 1, 2026, and early user reports suggest no significant engine performance issues. A truck driver in North Sumatra reported smooth operation with no mechanical complaints after switching to B50. This is a positive signal for Indonesia's palm oil industry and the government's strategic push to increase domestic CPO absorption through the biodiesel mandate.

medium.title: BP Fuel Station Cuts Petrol Prices Starting August 1, But Raises Diesel Price
medium.summary: BP Indonesia has reduced prices for its petrol products effective August 1, 2026: BP 92 dropped from Rp 16,670 to Rp 16,130 per liter, and BP Ultimate fell from Rp 17,240 to Rp 16,760 per liter, in line with Pertamina's price cuts. However, BP Ultimate Diesel rose from Rp 21,340 to Rp 21,910 per liter. These price changes are relevant for energy sector investors and businesses with significant fuel cost exposure.

medium.title: Allo Bank Posts Rp 130 Billion Net Profit in Q2 2026, Up 14% YoY
medium.summary: PT Allo Bank Indonesia Tbk (BBHI) reported a net profit of Rp 130 billion in Q2 2026, representing 14% year-on-year growth from Rp 114 billion in Q2 2025. Growth was driven by a 21% YoY increase in operating income to Rp 533 billion, with fee-based income surging 71% YoY to Rp 140 billion. The results demonstrate resilient performance amid a challenging macroeconomic environment, relevant for investors tracking digital banking stocks.

medium.title: RAJA's Profit Surges 88% to Rp 521 Billion in H1 2026
medium.summary: PT Rukun Raharja Tbk (RAJA) reported a strong H1 2026 net profit of US$28.9 million (~Rp 521.82 billion), up 88% from US$15.4 million in H1 2025, driven by full contribution from the Sengkang Gas Compressor project. Revenue grew a modest 3% to US$131.2 million, as the new project offset a decline in gas sales volumes caused by pipeline disruptions in Sumatra. The significant profit jump makes RAJA a notable performer in the energy sector for equity investors.

medium.title: Garuda Indonesia Speaks Out on State-Owned Airline Holding Plan with Pelita Air
medium.summary: PT Garuda Indonesia Tbk confirmed that a consolidation plan involving Pelita Air is currently under intensive review with shareholders and relevant stakeholders. The review covers strategic direction, structure, timeline, and implementation mechanisms as part of Garuda Indonesia Group's broader transformation agenda. While still in early stages, any consolidation of state-owned airlines could be a significant corporate action affecting Garuda's valuation and competitive positioning.

medium.title: KUR Loans Under Rp 100 Million Prohibited from Requiring Collateral
medium.summary: The Indonesian Ministry of MSMEs has reaffirmed that KUR (People's Business Credit) loans up to Rp 100 million must not require any additional collateral, and the public is urged to report violations including collateral demands, fee charges, or brokerage practices. The government emphasizes that no intermediary fees are needed to access KUR financing. This policy clarification is relevant for banks and financial institutions distributing KUR, as it signals stricter compliance enforcement in MSME lending.

medium.title: Rice Aid to Be Distributed Simultaneously on August 17 Independence Day
medium.summary: The National Food Agency (Bapanas) has officially tasked Bulog with distributing government food reserves (CPP) as rice assistance to over 33.2 million recipients, providing 10 kg each for the July–September 2026 period. The distribution is set to coincide with Indonesia's 81st Independence Day on August 17. This social safety net program aims to protect household purchasing power and stabilize national food prices, with implications for Bulog's operations and the broader rice market.

medium.title: Kadin Chief Reveals Indonesian-Made Components Used by Tesla, Airbus, and IKEA
medium.summary: Kadin Chairman Anindya Bakrie highlighted Indonesia's growing role as a key player in global supply chains, noting that Indonesian-made components are already integrated into products by global giants such as Tesla, Airbus, and IKEA. The remarks were made during a meeting between President Prabowo and Kadin at the Presidential Palace. This underscores Indonesia's manufacturing competitiveness and presents opportunities for investors in Indonesia's industrial and export sectors.

medium.title: Business Leaders Reveal Prabowo's Message After Meeting at Presidential Palace
medium.summary: President Prabowo met with Kadin leaders from central and regional levels at the Presidential Palace on July 31, urging national elites and business leaders to remain united amid uncertain global economic conditions. Business leaders responded positively, emphasizing compliance with laws and regulations and projecting a strong economic foundation to the world. The meeting signals continued government-business alignment, which could support investor confidence in Indonesia's economic stability.

medium.title: Garuda Indonesia Speaks Out on State-Owned Airline Holding Plan
medium.summary: PT Garuda Indonesia (Persero) Tbk has confirmed via a disclosure to the Indonesia Stock Exchange that a consolidation plan involving Pelita Air is currently under intensive study and discussion with shareholders and relevant parties. The review covers strategic direction, structure, stages, timeline, and implementation mechanisms aimed at strengthening the Garuda Indonesia Group ecosystem. Investors should monitor this development as a potential consolidation could materially reshape the state-owned aviation sector.

medium.title: KUR Loans Below Rp 100 Million Prohibited from Requiring Collateral
medium.summary: The Indonesian Ministry of SMEs has reaffirmed that Kredit Usaha Rakyat (KUR) loans with a ceiling up to Rp 100 million require no additional collateral of any kind, in line with the KUR Implementation Guidelines. The public is urged to report any violations including requests for collateral, fees, or brokerage practices. This regulatory clarification is relevant to banks distributing KUR and to small business owners seeking access to government-backed credit facilities.

medium.title: Rice Aid to Be Distributed Simultaneously on August 17 Independence Day
medium.summary: Indonesia's National Food Agency (Bapanas) has officially tasked Bulog with distributing government food reserves as rice aid to 33.24 million recipients, providing 10 kg per recipient covering July, August, and September 2026 allocations. The second phase of distribution will be launched simultaneously on August 17 to coincide with Indonesia's 81st Independence Day. This social safety net program aims to protect consumer purchasing power and strengthen national food stability, with significant implications for Bulog's operations and the broader food sector.

medium.title: Bakrie Electric Bus Issuer VKTR Records Rp 647 Billion in Sales, Rp 10 Billion Net Profit in H1 2026
medium.summary: PT VKTR Teknologi Mobilitas Tbk (VKTR), Bakrie Group's electric bus company, reported net sales of Rp 647 billion in the first half of 2026, a 56% year-on-year increase, driven by growth in commercial electric vehicles and the recovery of the national automotive industry. Operating profit surged 1,890% YoY to Rp 16 billion, while net profit grew 25% YoY to Rp 10 billion. The strong results highlight growing adoption of electric commercial vehicles in Indonesia and signal improving fundamentals for VKTR as a publicly listed EV player.

medium.title: Bank Mandiri and Telkom Aggressively Buy Back Shares as IHSG Weakens
medium.summary: Deputy House Speaker Sufmi Dasco Ahmad met with the BUMN Regulatory Board chairman, the State Secretary Minister, and leaders of state-owned banks (Himbara) to discuss capital market volatility and share buyback actions by state-owned enterprises. Officials acknowledged that Himbara bank fundamentals remain strong but that share prices have been dragged down by global market turbulence. The coordinated buyback effort by major BUMN companies such as Bank Mandiri and Telkom is intended to provide market support and restore investor confidence in Indonesian blue-chip stocks.
